ACCPPDE101.currentContent: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
ACCPPDE101.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

BENGATE102.currentContent: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
BENGATE102.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

DISDATA111.currentContent: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
DISDATA111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

GOSLAWJ111.currentContent: Studies human rights both as positive law and as philosophical claims. Students examine the UDHR, European and UN protection systems, monitoring institutions and landmark cases alongside natural law, natural rights, legal positivism and critiques of universality. Historical and philosophical texts frame debates about dignity, life and reproductive rights, punishment, religious freedom, expression and democracy. Close engagement with legal and philosophical arguments supports independent moral positions.
GOSLAWJ111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

GOSPOLI111.currentContent: Surveys political thought from classical antiquity to contemporary debates, including European and non-European thinkers. Students examine views of human nature, society, rights and authority in their historical contexts and compare their proposed solutions with current political problems. Close study of original texts, an individual essay and a group project developing a coherent political philosophy connect historical interpretation to normative argument.
GOSPOLI111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

GOSSOCI111.currentContent: Introduces sociological reasoning through classical theories, their historical settings and perspectives that address exclusions from the discipline. Students connect solidarity, modernity, identity, social boundaries, networks and stratification to race, gender, migration and inequality in education and work. An individual analysis applies a course concept to contemporary social life without original data collection. A group paper develops a sociological question and analyzes a social problem using theory and academic literature.
GOSSOCI111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

GOSSOCI212.currentContent: Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination. Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.
GOSSOCI212.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBCOGN112.currentContent: Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives. Brain anatomy and laboratory introductions support analysis of animal behaviour, research models and welfare. The second part connects regulatory behaviour and biological rhythms to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based disorder report apply neurobiological concepts while animal-research assignments examine reduction, refinement and replacement.
HCBCOGN112.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBCOGN212.currentContent: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
HCBCOGN212.finding: Description-only evidence supports neural perception/action mechanisms; fully considered, without inventing developmental teaching methods.

HCBCOGN311.currentContent: Deepens understanding of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and the experimental study of higher cognitive functions. Students examine attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control, social cognition, pain and consciousness, connecting brain function and dysfunction to behaviour. An attentional-blink experiment provides direct engagement with empirical work. A team research proposal requires literature analysis, a feasible experimental design and ethical reflection, supported by peer review.
HCBCOGN311.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBCOGN312.currentContent: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
HCBCOGN312.finding: Description-only evidence explicitly supports language acquisition, reading/dyslexia and experimental language study; fully considered as a strong language foundation. It does not teach the complete reading/spelling/multilingual instructional sequence.

HCBGATE102.currentContent: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
HCBGATE102.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC111.currentContent: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
HCBPSYC111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC211.currentContent: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
HCBPSYC211.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC212.currentContent: Examines mental health and psychopathology across the lifespan using a biopsychosocial perspective. Historical views, classification and assessment frame biological, psychological, cultural and social explanations of disorders and treatment. Case-based work applies diagnostic concepts to varied presentations. A structured literature-based essay investigates a focused mental-health question through explicit searching, source selection, evidence appraisal and synthesis, with optional use of PRISMA reporting tools.
HCBPSYC212.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC311.currentContent: Examines health and illness through interactions among biological, psychological and sociocultural factors. Health inequalities, behaviour and prevention lead into stress, symptoms, pain, medical consultation and treatment decisions. Chronic illness is considered from patients', families' and healthcare professionals' perspectives. Students analyze research, interventions and clinical cases, practice interviewing with attention to culture, and apply clinical-health formulation to understand support and quality of life in medical settings.
HCBPSYC311.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC312.currentContent: Introduces clinical psychological assessment and major psychotherapeutic approaches across the lifespan. Students study ethics, diagnostic systems, test reliability and validity, interviews, personality and cognitive assessment, then psychodynamic, behavioural, cognitive, humanistic, systemic and integrative treatments. Training sessions develop introductory administration, scoring and interpretation skills. A psychodiagnostic case report integrates findings and treatment recommendations, while self-monitoring examines developing clinical skills.
HCBPSYC312.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC313.currentContent: Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research. Students define review questions, search and select studies, extract and code findings, assess bias and compute effect sizes. Hands-on R work fits fixed- and random-effects models, examines heterogeneity and moderators, conducts meta-regression and investigates publication bias. A group project completes a small meta-analysis and presents its methods and results in a research poster.
HCBPSYC313.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC314.currentContent: Examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life through old age and death. Biological and environmental influences are considered alongside attachment, education, relationships, cultural differences and developmental psychopathology. Students connect theoretical perspectives to case studies, assessment and interventions at different life stages. A life-story interview with an adult over fifty applies developmental concepts through interviewing, analysis and a written report.
HCBPSYC314.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

HCBPSYC315.currentContent: Examines youth radicalization and educational prevention through psychology, education, sociology, political science and peace education. Models of radicalization and adolescent risk and protective factors lead into inclusive school climates, belonging, social-emotional learning, dialogue, media literacy and civic agency. Students translate primary research into teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit for an international school project, then revise the resources using feedback from intended recipients.
HCBPSYC315.finding: Actual youth prevention, inclusive school climate and evidence-informed teacher/youth resources strengthen educational relevance. They are not a sustained primary-school teaching/didactics curriculum.

MCCCOMM111.currentContent: Teaches rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication through classical history, theory and practice. Students study Greek and Roman rhetoric, the five canons, types of discourse, persuasive appeals, argumentation and fallacies. Written exercises, debates and public speeches develop invention, arrangement, style, memory and delivery. An applied project creates narrative and storytelling material for an immersive educational setting concerned with Zeeland's climate and community.
MCCCOMM111.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

MCCCOMM211.currentContent: Studies how linguistic choices produce meaning and interpretive effects, principally in literary texts but also in nonfiction. Students connect linguistic description to interpretation across grammar, discourse and cognition. Stylistic frameworks address foregrounding, dialogue, narration, modality, transitivity, deixis, schemas, construal and text worlds. Frequent analysis exercises lead to an original, research-supported stylistic analysis of a selected text.
MCCCOMM211.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.

MCCCOMM213.currentContent: Applies rhetoric through community-engaged work with local primary-school children. Students develop their own public-speaking, debating and storytelling skills, then design and iteratively refine age-appropriate teaching activities with school partners. On-site coaching and a final public-speaking event connect rhetorical education to civic participation and confidence. Structured reflection examines reciprocity, cultural sensitivity, personal development and the practical challenges of community-engaged teaching.
MCCCOMM213.finding: Actual primary-school rhetorical teaching, coaching, age-appropriate activity design and reflection are genuine educational contributions. They remain narrower than subject didactics across reading, spelling, handwriting, maths, world orientation, arts and multilingual teaching with sequenced placements.

MCCCOMM311.currentContent: Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work. Students study coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and verbal and nonverbal communication. Projects with the Delta Climate Centre and Vlissingen municipality develop communication encouraging sustainable and circular lifestyles. An individual research paper evaluates selected persuasion tools through literature review, field research diaries and reflective analysis of their use.
MCCCOMM311.finding: Read current evidence, not old cached approval. Substantive contribution retained within its stated subject scope; this course does not establish the missing sustained primary-school subject-didactics and supervised teaching sequence.
